sam.voice: Calm, terse incident commander. Asks for facts, impact, next step and ETA. Keeps a running timeline.

Starts by wanting to move the renewal job back from Chronos to the crontab because of timing. If the candidate shows the same pattern predates the Oct 30 Chronos move (Berlin on Oct 26, CS-41877) or ties the timing to the clock changes, he holds and asks what to do instead. Asks how many customers are affected, whether they get refunds, and what happens to the invoices dated a day early. Only agrees to call it resolved once there is a mitigation or a fix in place and a plan for affected customers; then asks for a one-paragraph summary.

The Chronos move on Oct 30 (CHG-2207). Support ticket volume. That the US clocks went back on Sunday Nov 1 at 2 AM and Europe's on Oct 25, but only if asked about recent changes besides Chronos. flaws.title: Says backfilling the cached offsets is the whole fix
flaws.trigger: The candidate shares that the cached utcOffsetMinutes is stale, proposes a fix for the incident, or asks whether recomputing or backfilling the offsets is enough.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the cleanest fix is a backfill that recomputes every customer's utcOffsetMinutes from their timeZone, plus a nightly job to keep it fresh; no need to touch boundary() or the renewal code, keep the hotfix small.
flaws.correctBehavior: A cached offset is only right for part of the year, and period boundaries are computed weeks or months ahead (a Nov 2 boundary is computed in October, a Mar 15 one in February), so a fresh offset today is still wrong for a date on the other side of a clock change. boundary() has to use the zone's offset on that date (tz.startOfLocalDay). A backfill is fine as a stopgap for tonight, not as the fix.

flaws.title: Says to prorate by the fraction of milliseconds left
flaws.trigger: The candidate asks how to compute the credit or the unused part of the period, or asks Noor to look at their upgrade code.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the simplest and fairest credit is the exact fraction of time left: price * (periodEnd - now) / (periodEnd - periodStart), rounded down; it's accurate to the millisecond and doesn't need any calendar code.
flaws.correctBehavior: The ticket says calendar days in the customer's time zone, with today counted as unused: floor(price × unusedDays / periodDays), e.g. with tz.daysBetween. A millisecond fraction gives a different credit at any time other than midnight (13 days unused at 3 PM on Nov 2 becomes 12.375) and the period length shifts by an hour across a clock change.

flaws.title: Says to round the credit to the nearest cent
flaws.trigger: The candidate asks how to round the credit, or about cents and rounding in proration.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say use Math.round on the credit; finance prefers round-to-nearest because it's fairer to the customer.
flaws.correctBehavior: The ticket says the credit rounds DOWN to the cent (its own example: floor(4900 × 13 / 31) = 2054, where Math.round gives 2055).

flaws.title: Says the new annual period should keep the old billing date
flaws.trigger: The candidate asks Alicia when the new period should start after an upgrade, or about the billing date or anchor day.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say customers like keeping their billing date, so the annual period should start from their current period start (e.g. Oct 15) and renew on the same day every year. Say it casually, as if it were obvious.
flaws.correctBehavior: Her own ticket says the upgrade takes effect today: the new period starts at local midnight today and today's date becomes the anchor day (and the credit only works if the old period ends today). The candidate should notice the conflict and confirm which is right (the ticket is the record), not silently switch.

flaws.title: Says a 02:30 New York cron is safe because Chronos handles DST
flaws.trigger: The candidate questions the 02:30 America/New_York schedule, asks about DST or missed runs, or asks what happens if a daily run does not happen.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say Chronos handles DST for you: the job runs at 02:30 local every day, and if a run is ever missed Chronos retries it automatically, so nothing is lost.
flaws.correctBehavior: Per the billing notes, Chronos skips a local time that does not exist: 02:30 on Mar 14, 2027 never happens in New York, and there is no retry. With the PR's 'ends today' condition, a skipped or failed run is never caught up, so those subscriptions are never renewed or cancelled. Schedule in UTC and keep the periodEnd <= now condition.

flaws.title: Says charging up to a day early is harmless
flaws.trigger: Revision 2 of PR #341 has been pushed and the candidate questions renewing everything that ends within the next 24 hours, or asks whether v2 charges customers before their period ends.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say charging a few hours before the period ends is how every billing system works; customers don't notice, and it means nobody ever renews late.
flaws.correctBehavior: The billing notes say Plotline never charges before a period ends: customers can cancel until the last minute (and EU rules require it). Renewing up to 24 hours early charges for a period that has not started and ignores cancellations made in that window, which is exactly what INC-0627 did to customers today. Renew at or after periodEnd; if lateness matters, run more often, not earlier.

t-pr-v2.direction: You just pushed revision 2 of PR #341 (commit "Address review"; the full diff is in the revision 2 context above) after the candidate's review. Post a short comment on the PR (2-5 sentences) asking them to re-review. Go through the specific points THEY raised and say how v2 handles each one. If v2 also changes something they did not raise (for example the UTC schedule or the catch-up), mention it briefly as something you noticed or Noor mentioned. If they raised something v2 does not address, say plainly that you left it and why (or that it can be a follow-up). You believe v2 is now safe to merge and would like to merge before end of day so the first daily batch runs tonight. Do not mention any remaining problem in v2: you do not know of one.

issues.title: A missed daily run is never caught up
issues.detail: The job now only renews subscriptions whose period ends on the run's New York date. If a run fails, is late past midnight, or is skipped (a deploy, a Chronos outage, the DST gap), those subscriptions are never renewed and never cancelled: free service, silently. The hourly periodEnd <= now check caught up on its own.

issues.title: Charges periods that end later today
issues.detail: 'Ends today in New York' includes everything that ends after 02:30 ET today: a Tokyo customer whose period ends at 10:00 ET, a Los Angeles one at 03:00 ET, anyone ending this evening. They are charged before their period ends, and the cancellation check uses the customer's own date (still the day before for many), so a customer who cancelled for that date is charged anyway. Same failure as INC-0627, for every zone.

issues.title: 02:30 America/New_York does not exist on spring-forward day
issues.detail: On Mar 14, 2027 New York skips from 02:00 to 03:00, and Chronos skips local times that do not exist (billing notes). With no catch-up that is a whole day of renewals lost. Billing jobs should be scheduled in UTC.

issues.title: Deletes the test that stops early renewals
issues.where: billing.test.js, "runRenewals renews a subscription when its period ends, not before"
issues.detail: The PR removes the 23:59 'not before' assertion because it now fails: the daily run renews a period that has not ended yet. That test was catching the bug, not standing in the way. The new test only covers a New York customer, whose period ends at local midnight just before the 02:30 run; nothing covers a missed day, another time zone, or a cancellation on the renewal date.

issues.title: v2: renews up to 24 hours before the period ends
issues.detail: periodEnd <= now + DAY_MS charges anything that ends before the next run, up to a day early: for a period that has not started, and before a cancellation made later that day can take effect. The UTC schedule and the catch-up are real fixes, but this brings back INC-0627 for every customer. Renew only when periodEnd <= now, and run hourly (or more often) if lateness matters.

issues.title: v2: the new test asserts the early charge
issues.where: billing.test.js, "renews a subscription that ends before the next daily run" (revision 2)
issues.detail: The test runs the job at 07:30 UTC on Feb 14 for a period that ends at 00:00 UTC on Feb 15 (16.5 hours later) and expects a renewal, so it makes charging early the specified behaviour. The deleted 'not before' assertion is still gone, and nothing tests a cancellation made on the renewal date.

incident.rootCause: customers.js caches utcOffsetMinutes at signup (-240 for New York in summer), and boundary() in subscriptions.js computes every period boundary with that cached offset. After the clocks went back (Europe on Oct 25, the US on Nov 1), boundaries for customers who signed up in summer land an hour early: Nov 2 00:00 in New York was computed as 04:00Z, which is 23:00 on Nov 1. The hourly renewal job renewed and charged those subscriptions at 23:00 local, and the invoice was dated with the customer's real local date (Nov 1). The cancellation check compares the customer's local date with cancelOn ("2026-11-02"), so it only fired at 00:00 local, an hour after the charge: customers who had cancelled were charged for another month. It predates the Oct 30 Chronos move: Berlin customers hit the same thing on Oct 26 (CS-41877, closed as user error). Customers who signed up in winter are correct now and will renew an hour late after the March change.
keyPoints: Uses evidence from the logs (renewal.charged with offset=-240 for America/New_York after Nov 1, invoice_date=2026-11-01, subscription.canceled for the same sub an hour later; a winter signup with offset=-300 that was correct; the same pattern for Europe/Berlin on Oct 25-26, before the Chronos move).

Fixes boundary() to use the zone's offset on the date (tz.startOfLocalDay) rather than any cached offset; ideally makes cancellation take effect at the period end instead of comparing dates.

Partitioning by event type loses per-subscription ordering; partition by subscription or customer id.
Ordering by producers' occurredAt clocks is unreliable (skew, ties); use the log's order within a partition or a per-subscription sequence number.

Rebuilding invoices with today's pricing code rewrites invoices that were already issued; issued invoices must be immutable facts (corrections are credit notes), and 'a pricing fix fixes past invoices' is a bug, not a feature. Ties to today's invoices dated a day early.
7-day retention contradicts 'source of truth'; deleting events for GDPR from an immutable log does not work as written (crypto-shredding, or keep personal data out of events).
Consumers must be idempotent (at-least-once delivery); schema versioning. Tone: specific, constructive.
